title: Bees Among the Flowers
devanagari: दूताहूत इतस्ततो भ्रमति खे भृङ्गोऽलिसंख्यां वद॥
iast: pañcāṃśo 'li-kulāt kadambam agamat tryaṃśaḥ śilīndhraṃ tayor
dūtāhūta itas tato bhramati khe bhṛṅgo 'li-saṃkhyāṃ vada ||
translation: From a swarm of bees, one fifth flew to a kadamba flower and one third to a śilīndhra. Three times the difference of these two went to a kuṭaja, O deer-eyed one. One bee was left, swinging to and fro in the sky, drawn at the same moment by the fragrance of the ketakī and the jasmine, like a lover called by two messengers. Tell me, dear one, the number of bees.
translation_hi: भौंरों के झुंड का पाँचवाँ भाग कदंब पर गया और तीसरा भाग शिलींध्र पर। हे मृगनयनी, इन दोनों के अंतर का तीन गुना कुटज पर गया। एक भौंरा बचा जो केतकी और मालती की सुगंध से एक साथ बुलाए जाने पर, दो दूतों से बुलाए प्रेमी की तरह, आकाश में इधर उधर डोल रहा है। हे प्रिये, भौंरों की संख्या बताओ।

words.note: Same as triguṇita in the peacock verse.
Also in the first bee verse.
Same ending as the first bee verse.

grammar: Aorist past: अगमत् 'went', another past tense (compare चकार and अपतत्).
Ablative 'from': अलिकुलात् 'from the swarm', like बिलात् 'from the hole'.
Visarga to ś: विश्लेषः + त्रिगुणः → विश्लेषस्त्रिगुणः (स् before त), and तयोः + विश्लेषः → तयोर्विश्लेषः (र् before a voiced sound).
Poetry in maths: the lone bee is compared to a lover torn between two messengers. Bhaskara never lets the numbers be dull.
question: How many bees were in the swarm?
solution:
Let the swarm be x. Kadamba: x/5. Śilīndhra: x/3. Kuṭaja: 3 × (x/3 − x/5) = 2x/5. One bee is left.

x/5 + x/3 + 2x/5 + 1 = x  ⟹  (3 + 5 + 6)x/15 + 1 = x  ⟹  x/15 = 1  ⟹  x = 15 bees

Check: 3 + 5 + 6 + 1 = 15

Science link: a linear equation with fractions, solved by clearing denominators with their least common multiple, 15. Bhaskara also solves it with iṣṭa-karma, the method of false position from the necklace verse.
